+# Leakage-free benchmarking of electronic noses for beef freshness
+
+Reproduction package for the manuscript
+
+> E. C. Ozkat, "Leakage-Free Benchmarking of Electronic Noses for Beef Freshness:
+> A Signal-Richness Criterion for Model Selection", *Foods* (under review, foods-4454911).
+
+Everything needed to regenerate every table and figure in the paper is here: the analysis
+code, the fold definitions and seeds, the raw per-fold result files, the stored
+out-of-fold predictions, and a verification script that recomputes all reported numbers
+from those stored predictions.
+
+The three source datasets are **not** redistributed here; they are public and are downloaded
+from their original repositories in one step (see [`data/README.md`](data/README.md)).
+
+---
+
+## Quick start
+
+```bash
+git clone https://github.com/eco160/beef-enose-leakage-free
+cd beef-enose-leakage-free
+python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
+pip install -r requirements.txt
+
+# 1. download the three public datasets into data/ (see data/README.md), then:
+python code/data_prep.py            # builds data/combined_B.csv and data/combined_A.csv
+
+# 2. reproduce the main results (~20 min, CPU only)
+python code/revision_runs.py        # core benchmark, ablations, transfer, threshold
+python code/nested_sensor_selection.py   # nested per-fold sensor selection (~45 min)
+python code/basic_reviewer_analyses.py   # dataset structure, autocorrelation, MMD
+python code/classical_window_loco.py     # classical baselines on the same windows
+python code/rethink_coffee.py            # heater-profile foil (~2.5 h)
+
+# 3. verify: recomputes every reported number from the stored predictions
+python code/verify_results.py       # 46 checks without the datasets, 51 with them; 0 failures
+```
+
+All experiments run on CPU. No GPU is required.
+
+## Evaluation protocol in one paragraph
+
+The beef corpus contains 12 independent sensor acquisitions ("cuts"), each 2220 minutes at
+one reading per minute. Sixty-minute windows are taken at an eight-minute stride, giving
+3252 windows, and each window is labelled by its final time step. Cross-validation is
+**leave-one-cut-out**: in each of the 12 folds, every window from one named cut forms the
+test set and the remaining eleven cuts form the training set, so no window is ever split
+across the boundary. The fold definition is therefore fully determined by the cut name — no
+random assignment is involved and no fold file is needed. TVC is never supplied as an input
+feature to any classifier. Seeds are set per fold (`torch.manual_seed(1000 + k)`,
+`np.random.seed(1000 + k)`) so that every model arm shares an initialisation stream and
+paired comparisons are exact.
+
+## Where each result comes from
+
+| Manuscript item | Script | Result file |
+|---|---|---|
+| Table 3, Table 4 (core LOCO comparison) | `revision_runs.py` | `results/revision_runs.json` → `A_core_loco` |
+| Table 5 (representation vs architecture, TVC-head ablation) | `revision_runs.py` | `results/revision_runs.json` → `A_core_loco.arms` |
+| Table 6, Figure 5 (leakage and protocol inflation) | `revision_runs.py`, `run_classical_loco.py` | `results/revision_runs.json` → `F_protocol_inflation`; `results/classical_loco_B.json` |
+| Table 7 (transfer, reduced array, deployment) | `revision_runs.py`, `nested_sensor_selection.py` | `results/revision_runs.json` → `D_transfer`; `results/nested_sensor_selection.json` |
+| Figure 6 (selection stability) | `nested_sensor_selection.py` | `results/nested_sensor_selection.json` → `selection_stability` |
+| Table 8 (conservative operating point) | `revision_runs.py` | `results/revision_runs.json` → `E_conservative_threshold` |
+| Table 9, Figure 7 (heater-profile foil, dose-response) | `rethink_coffee.py` | `results/rethink_coffee.json` |
+| Figure 4 (TVC calibration) | `revision_runs.py` | `results/revision_oof.npz` |
+| Section 3.1 dataset structure, Section 3.3 autocorrelation, Section 5 MMD | `basic_reviewer_analyses.py` | `results/basic_reviewer_analyses.json` |
+| Classical baselines quoted in Section 4.1 | `classical_window_loco.py` | `results/classical_window_loco.json` |
+| Verification of all of the above | `verify_results.py` | `results/verification.json` |
+
+`results/revision_oof.npz` holds the pooled out-of-fold predictions (true labels, cut
+identifiers, predicted classes, predicted class probabilities and predicted TVC for both
+models), from which every pooled metric, the calibration figure and the threshold sweep can
+be regenerated without retraining anything.
+
+## Software environment
+
+Pinned in `requirements.txt` and used for every number in the paper:
+
+Python 3.12.3 · NumPy 1.26.4 · pandas 2.3.3 · scikit-learn 1.2.2 · XGBoost 3.2.0 ·
+LightGBM 4.6.0 · PyTorch 2.6.0 (CPU) · SciPy 1.17.1
+
+Two notes on reproducibility across environments. XGBoost version affects the tree results:
+the submitted version of the manuscript used XGBoost 1.6.2 and reported a gradient-boosted
+tree macro-F1 of 0.660, whereas 3.2.0 gives 0.684 on identical folds and features. The
+PyTorch results are stable across 1.13.1 and 2.6.0 (fold 1 macro-F1 0.582 in both).
+`PyWavelets` is optional and needed only for the wavelet-denoising front-end, which was
+evaluated but not used in the reported configuration.
+
+## Repository layout
+
+```
+code/       analysis scripts (see the table above)
+results/    result JSONs, stored out-of-fold predictions, run logs
+data/       download instructions and checksums; datasets are not redistributed
+```
+

+

+See `CITATION.cff`. Please cite the manuscript above and the three source datasets.

+# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
+"""Descriptive analyses for the Foods revision (no model fitting).
+
+Part 1 (Reviewer 1.2) — inter-cut heterogeneity and within-cut autocorrelation:
+  * TVC evolution rate per cut (log10 CFU/g per hour, OLS slope over the 2220 min),
+    between-cut variance and coefficient of variation, time spent in each grade,
+    the minute at which each cut crosses TVC = 5.0 (the spoilage threshold).
+  * Within-cut autocorrelation of the sensor channels at lags 1, 8 (the window stride),
+    60 (the window length) and 240 min, plus the integrated autocorrelation time and the
+    implied effective sample size. This is the quantity that makes a random split optimistic
+    and leave-one-cut-out conservative.
+
+Part 2 (Reviewer 1.5) — quantified response-distribution shift between the primary corpus
+  (B, 11 sensors) and the independent corpus (A, 9 sensors) over the 9 shared channels:
+  * per-channel standardised mean difference and scale ratio,
+  * per-channel and joint maximum mean discrepancy (MMD^2, RBF kernel, median heuristic)
+    with a permutation test,
+  * the same quantities after per-cut R/R0 baseline referencing, to show how much of the
+    shift a simple calibration transfer removes.
+
+Writes results/basic_reviewer_analyses.json.
+"""
+import os, json
+import numpy as np
+import pandas as pd
+
+HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
+DATA = os.path.join(HERE, "..", "data")
+RES = os.path.join(HERE, "..", "results")
+
+SENS_B = ["MQ135", "MQ136", "MQ137", "MQ138", "MQ2", "MQ3", "MQ4", "MQ5", "MQ6", "MQ8", "MQ9"]
+SENS_A = ["MQ135", "MQ136", "MQ2", "MQ3", "MQ4", "MQ5", "MQ6", "MQ8", "MQ9"]  # 9 shared
+CLASS_NAMES = ["excellent", "good", "acceptable", "spoiled"]
+RNG = np.random.RandomState(42)
+
+
+def read_csv_safe(path):
+    with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
+        return pd.read_csv(fh)
+
+
+# ----------------------------------------------------------------- Part 1
+def ols_slope(t, y):
+    tc = t - t.mean()
+    return float((tc * (y - y.mean())).sum() / (tc ** 2).sum())
+
+
+def acf(x, lag):
+    if lag >= len(x):
+        return float("nan")
+    a, b = x[:-lag], x[lag:]
+    a = a - a.mean(); b = b - b.mean()
+    d = np.sqrt((a ** 2).sum() * (b ** 2).sum())
+    return float((a * b).sum() / d) if d > 0 else float("nan")
+
+
+def integrated_act(x, maxlag=600):
+    """Sum of the autocorrelation function to its first zero crossing (Sokal's window)."""
+    s = 1.0
+    for lag in range(1, min(maxlag, len(x) - 1)):
+        r = acf(x, lag)
+        if not np.isfinite(r) or r <= 0:
+            break
+        s += 2 * r
+    return float(s)
+
+
+def part1_heterogeneity(dfB):
+    per_cut, rates = [], []
+    for cut, sub in dfB.groupby("cut", sort=False):
+        sub = sub.sort_values("Minute")
+        t = sub["Minute"].values.astype(float)
+        tvc = sub["TVC"].values.astype(float)
+        slope_per_min = ols_slope(t, tvc)
+        lab = sub["Label"].astype(int).values
+        cross = np.where(tvc >= 5.0)[0]
+        counts = {CLASS_NAMES[i - 1]: int((lab == i).sum()) for i in (1, 2, 3, 4)}
+        rec = {
+            "cut": str(cut),
+            "n_min": int(len(sub)),
+            "tvc_start": float(tvc[0]), "tvc_end": float(tvc[-1]),
+            "tvc_span": float(tvc[-1] - tvc[0]),
+            "rate_log10_per_hour": round(slope_per_min * 60, 5),
+            "minute_cross_tvc5": int(t[cross[0]]) if len(cross) else None,
+            "minutes_per_grade": counts,
+        }
+        per_cut.append(rec)
+        rates.append(rec["rate_log10_per_hour"])
+    rates = np.asarray(rates, float)
+    summary = {
+        "n_cuts": int(len(rates)),
+        "rate_mean_log10_per_hour": float(rates.mean()),
+        "rate_sd_log10_per_hour": float(rates.std(ddof=1)),
+        "rate_cv_percent": float(100 * rates.std(ddof=1) / rates.mean()),
+        "rate_min": float(rates.min()), "rate_max": float(rates.max()),
+        "rate_fold_range": float(rates.max() / rates.min()),
+        "between_cut_variance": float(rates.var(ddof=1)),
+    }
+    return {"per_cut": per_cut, "rate_summary": summary}
+
+
+def part1_autocorrelation(dfB):
+    lags = [1, 8, 60, 240]
+    per_sensor = {s: {("lag%d" % L): [] for L in lags} for s in SENS_B}
+    act_per_sensor = {s: [] for s in SENS_B}
+    tvc_lag = {("lag%d" % L): [] for L in lags}
+    for cut, sub in dfB.groupby("cut", sort=False):
+        sub = sub.sort_values("Minute")
+        for s in SENS_B:
+            x = sub[s].values.astype(float)
+            for L in lags:
+                per_sensor[s]["lag%d" % L].append(acf(x, L))
+            act_per_sensor[s].append(integrated_act(x))
+        tv = sub["TVC"].values.astype(float)
+        for L in lags:
+            tvc_lag["lag%d" % L].append(acf(tv, L))
+    out = {"lags_min": lags, "per_sensor_mean_acf": {}, "per_sensor_integrated_act": {}}
+    for s in SENS_B:
+        out["per_sensor_mean_acf"][s] = {k: round(float(np.nanmean(v)), 4)
+                                         for k, v in per_sensor[s].items()}
+        out["per_sensor_integrated_act"][s] = round(float(np.mean(act_per_sensor[s])), 1)
+    out["tvc_mean_acf"] = {k: round(float(np.nanmean(v)), 4) for k, v in tvc_lag.items()}
+    tau = float(np.mean([np.mean(act_per_sensor[s]) for s in SENS_B]))
+    n_per_cut = int(dfB.groupby("cut").size().mean())
+    out["mean_integrated_act_min"] = round(tau, 1)
+    out["effective_n_per_cut"] = round(n_per_cut / tau, 1)
+    out["nominal_n_per_cut"] = n_per_cut
+    out["note"] = ("Effective sample size = nominal / integrated autocorrelation time. "
+                   "A random split over rows therefore trains and tests on near-duplicates; "
+                   "leave-one-cut-out removes the entire correlated block.")
+    return out
+
+
+# ----------------------------------------------------------------- Part 2
+def rbf_mmd2(Xs, Ys, gamma=None, n=1500, rs=RNG):
+    """Unbiased MMD^2 with an RBF kernel; median-heuristic bandwidth on the pooled sample."""
+    Xs = Xs[rs.choice(len(Xs), min(n, len(Xs)), replace=False)]
+    Ys = Ys[rs.choice(len(Ys), min(n, len(Ys)), replace=False)]
+    Z = np.vstack([Xs, Ys])
+    sq = (Z ** 2).sum(1)
+    d2 = np.maximum(sq[:, None] + sq[None, :] - 2 * (Z @ Z.T), 0.0)   # memory-safe pairwise
+    if gamma is None:
+        med = np.median(d2[d2 > 0])
+        gamma = 1.0 / med if med > 0 else 1.0
+    K = np.exp(-gamma * d2)
+    nx, ny = len(Xs), len(Ys)
+    Kxx = K[:nx, :nx]; Kyy = K[nx:, nx:]; Kxy = K[:nx, nx:]
+    mmd2 = (Kxx.sum() - np.trace(Kxx)) / (nx * (nx - 1)) \
+         + (Kyy.sum() - np.trace(Kyy)) / (ny * (ny - 1)) \
+         - 2 * Kxy.mean()
+    return float(mmd2), float(gamma), K, nx, ny
+
+
+def mmd_perm_p(K, nx, ny, mmd2, n_perm=200, rs=RNG):
+    N = nx + ny
+    cnt = 0
+    for _ in range(n_perm):
+        idx = rs.permutation(N)
+        a, b = idx[:nx], idx[nx:]
+        Kaa = K[np.ix_(a, a)]; Kbb = K[np.ix_(b, b)]; Kab = K[np.ix_(a, b)]
+        m = (Kaa.sum() - np.trace(Kaa)) / (nx * (nx - 1)) \
+          + (Kbb.sum() - np.trace(Kbb)) / (ny * (ny - 1)) - 2 * Kab.mean()
+        cnt += (m >= mmd2)
+    return float((cnt + 1) / (n_perm + 1))
+
+
+def rr0(df, sensors, time_col, bwin=30):
+    """Per-cut R/R0 referencing: divide each channel by its own first-30-minute mean."""
+    parts = []
+    for cut, sub in df.groupby("cut", sort=False):
+        sub = sub.sort_values(time_col).copy()
+        r0 = sub[sensors].iloc[:bwin].mean(axis=0) + 1e-6
+        sub[sensors] = sub[sensors] / r0
+        parts.append(sub)
+    return pd.concat(parts, ignore_index=True)
+
+
+def part2_shift(dfB, dfA):
+    out = {}
+    for tag, (B, A) in {"raw": (dfB, dfA),
+                        "rr0": (rr0(dfB, SENS_A, "Minute"), rr0(dfA, SENS_A, "minute"))}.items():
+        Xb = B[SENS_A].values.astype(float)
+        Xa = A[SENS_A].values.astype(float)
+        # per-channel descriptive shift, standardised by the primary corpus
+        per_ch = {}
+        for j, s in enumerate(SENS_A):
+            mb, sb = Xb[:, j].mean(), Xb[:, j].std() + 1e-9
+            ma, sa = Xa[:, j].mean(), Xa[:, j].std() + 1e-9
+            m2, g2, K1, n1, n2 = rbf_mmd2(Xb[:, [j]], Xa[:, [j]])
+            per_ch[s] = {
+                "mean_B": round(float(mb), 3), "mean_A": round(float(ma), 3),
+                "standardised_mean_diff": round(float((ma - mb) / sb), 3),
+                "scale_ratio_A_over_B": round(float(sa / sb), 3),
+                "mmd2": round(m2, 4),
+            }
+        # joint shift on the z-scored (by B) 9-channel vector
+        mu, sd = Xb.mean(0), Xb.std(0) + 1e-9
+        Zb, Za = (Xb - mu) / sd, (Xa - mu) / sd
+        m2, gam, K, n1, n2 = rbf_mmd2(Zb, Za)
+        p = mmd_perm_p(K, n1, n2, m2)
+        out[tag] = {
+            "per_channel": per_ch,
+            "joint_mmd2": round(m2, 4),
+            "joint_mmd": round(float(np.sqrt(max(m2, 0))), 4),
+            "gamma_median_heuristic": round(gam, 6),
+            "perm_p": p,
+            "n_B": int(len(Xb)), "n_A": int(len(Xa)),
+        }
+    out["ranked_by_mmd2_raw"] = sorted(
+        out["raw"]["per_channel"], key=lambda s: -out["raw"]["per_channel"][s]["mmd2"])
+    out["note"] = ("MMD^2 is unbiased, RBF kernel, median-heuristic bandwidth, 1500 rows "
+                   "subsampled per corpus; permutation p over 200 relabellings. "
+                   "'rr0' repeats everything after per-cut R/R0 baseline referencing.")
+    return out
+
+
+def main():
+    dfB = read_csv_safe(os.path.join(DATA, "combined_B.csv"))
+    dfA = read_csv_safe(os.path.join(DATA, "combined_A.csv"))
+    out = {
+        "datasets": {"B_rows": int(len(dfB)), "B_cuts": int(dfB["cut"].nunique()),
+                     "A_rows": int(len(dfA)), "A_cuts": int(dfA["cut"].nunique()),
+                     "shared_sensors": SENS_A},
+        "inter_cut_heterogeneity": part1_heterogeneity(dfB),
+        "within_cut_autocorrelation": part1_autocorrelation(dfB),
+        "domain_shift_B_vs_A": part2_shift(dfB, dfA),
+    }
+    os.makedirs(RES, exist_ok=True)
+    with open(os.path.join(RES, "basic_reviewer_analyses.json"), "w") as fh:
+        json.dump(out, fh, indent=2)
+
+    rs = out["inter_cut_heterogeneity"]["rate_summary"]
+    ac = out["within_cut_autocorrelation"]
+    ds = out["domain_shift_B_vs_A"]
+    print("TVC rate: %.4f +/- %.4f log10/h  (CV %.1f%%, %.1fx spread across cuts)" % (
+        rs["rate_mean_log10_per_hour"], rs["rate_sd_log10_per_hour"],
+        rs["rate_cv_percent"], rs["rate_fold_range"]))
+    print("mean lag-1 sensor ACF: %.4f | lag-60: %.4f" % (
+        np.mean([v["lag1"] for v in ac["per_sensor_mean_acf"].values()]),
+        np.mean([v["lag60"] for v in ac["per_sensor_mean_acf"].values()])))
+    print("integrated ACT %.0f min -> effective n %.1f per cut (nominal %d)" % (
+        ac["mean_integrated_act_min"], ac["effective_n_per_cut"], ac["nominal_n_per_cut"]))
+    print("joint MMD^2 raw %.4f (p=%.3f) -> after R/R0 %.4f (p=%.3f)" % (
+        ds["raw"]["joint_mmd2"], ds["raw"]["perm_p"],
+        ds["rr0"]["joint_mmd2"], ds["rr0"]["perm_p"]))
+    print("channels ranked by shift:", ds["ranked_by_mmd2_raw"])
+    print("Saved results/basic_reviewer_analyses.json")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
+"""Classical baselines on the SAME window features, folds and stack as the main comparison.
+
+The submitted manuscript quoted random-forest, LightGBM and logistic-regression figures from
+a per-timestep run on the previous software stack. This re-runs them window-level, so the
+sentence "other classical models under the same protocol" is literally true.
+Writes results/classical_window_loco.json.
+"""
+import os, json, time
+import numpy as np, pandas as pd
+from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
+from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
+from sklearn.neural_network import MLPClassifier
+from sklearn.svm import SVC
+from sklearn.neighbors import KNeighborsClassifier
+from sklearn.pipeline import make_pipeline
+from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
+from sklearn.metrics import f1_score, accuracy_score
+from lightgbm import LGBMClassifier
+from mscnn_attention import read_csv_safe, make_windows, SENS_B, DATA, RES
+from rethink_beef import win_features
+
+MODELS = {
+    "RandomForest": lambda: RandomForestClassifier(400, random_state=42, n_jobs=-1),
+    "LightGBM": lambda: LGBMClassifier(n_estimators=400, max_depth=6, learning_rate=0.08,
+                                       subsample=0.9, random_state=42, n_jobs=-1, verbose=-1),
+    "LogisticRegression": lambda: make_pipeline(StandardScaler(),
+                                                LogisticRegression(max_iter=2000, random_state=42)),
+    "SVC-RBF": lambda: make_pipeline(StandardScaler(), SVC(random_state=42)),
+    "KNN": lambda: make_pipeline(StandardScaler(), KNeighborsClassifier()),
+    "MLP-sklearn": lambda: make_pipeline(StandardScaler(),
+                                         MLPClassifier((128, 64), max_iter=600, random_state=42)),
+}
+
+def main():
+    df = read_csv_safe(os.path.join(DATA, "combined_B.csv"))
+    X, yc, _, g = make_windows(df, SENS_B, 60, 8)
+    F = win_features(X); cuts = list(pd.unique(g))
+    out = {"protocol": "LOCO, 12 folds, 60-min windows / 8-min stride, 55 summary features"}
+    for name, ctor in MODELS.items():
+        t0 = time.time(); f1s, accs = [], []
+        for c in cuts:
+            te = g == c; tr = ~te

+# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
+"""Tuned position-aware MS-CNN-Attention for BME688 heater-profile odour classification
+(CoffeePow-4 / Aroma-7). Multi-scale conv + squeeze-excitation + learned positional
+embedding + transformer + position-preserving head. Compared to XGB under stratified
+5-fold x 3 seeds (macro-F1). Target: beat XGB and approach ConvTran's 0.964 on CoffeePow.
+"""
+import os, json, numpy as np, pandas as pd, torch, torch.nn as nn
+from sklearn.model_selection import StratifiedKFold
+from sklearn.metrics import f1_score, accuracy_score
+from xgboost import XGBClassifier
+
+HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
+DATA = os.path.join(HERE, "..", "data"); RES = os.path.join(HERE, "..", "results")
+
+def load(name, L=10):
+    with open(os.path.join(DATA, name)) as fh: df = pd.read_csv(fh)
+    r = df["Resistance Gassensor"].values.astype(np.float64); y = df["label"].values.astype(int)
+    n = len(df)//L
+    return np.log10(r[:n*L].reshape(n, L)+1.0).astype(np.float32), y[:n*L].reshape(n, L)[:, 0]
+
+class SE(nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self, c, r=4):
+        super().__init__(); self.fc = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(c, c//r), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(c//r, c), nn.Sigmoid())
+    def forward(self, x): return x * self.fc(x.mean(-1)).unsqueeze(-1)
+
+class MSCNNAttn(nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self, ncls, L=10, d=64):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.b1 = nn.Conv1d(1, 24, 3, padding=1); self.b2 = nn.Conv1d(1, 24, 5, padding=2)
+        self.b3 = nn.Conv1d(1, 24, 7, padding=3)
+        C = 72
+        self.bn = nn.BatchNorm1d(C); self.act = nn.ReLU(); self.se = SE(C)
+        self.proj = nn.Conv1d(C, d, 1); self.pos = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(1, L, d)*0.02)
+        enc = nn.TransformerEncoderLayer(d, 4, d*2, dropout=0.1, batch_first=True)
+        self.tr = nn.TransformerEncoder(enc, 2)
+        self.head = nn.Sequential(nn.Flatten(), nn.Linear(d*L, 128), nn.ReLU(), nn.Dropout(0.3),
+                                  nn.Linear(128, 64), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(64, ncls))
+    def forward(self, x):
+        h = self.se(self.act(self.bn(torch.cat([self.b1(x), self.b2(x), self.b3(x)], 1))))
+        h = self.proj(h).transpose(1, 2) + self.pos        # (B,L,d) position-aware
+        h = self.tr(h)
+        return self.head(h)
+
+def train_eval(Xtr, ytr, Xte, ncls, epochs=90, jitter=0.02):
+    mu, sd = Xtr.mean(0, keepdims=True), Xtr.std(0, keepdims=True)+1e-6
+    Xtr, Xte = (Xtr-mu)/sd, (Xte-mu)/sd
+    cw = np.bincount(ytr, minlength=ncls).astype(np.float32); cw = cw.sum()/(ncls*np.maximum(cw, 1))
+    net = MSCNNAttn(ncls); opt = torch.optim.Adam(net.parameters(), 1.2e-3, weight_decay=1e-4)
+    sch = torch.optim.lr_scheduler.CosineAnnealingLR(opt, epochs)
+    ce = nn.CrossEntropyLoss(weight=torch.tensor(cw))
+    Xt = torch.tensor(Xtr).unsqueeze(1); yt = torch.tensor(ytr).long(); n = len(Xt); bs = 128
+    for ep in range(epochs):
+        net.train(); perm = torch.randperm(n)
+        for i in range(0, n, bs):
+            idx = perm[i:i+bs]; xb = Xt[idx]
+            if jitter: xb = xb + torch.randn_like(xb)*jitter     # light noise augmentation
+            opt.zero_grad(); ce(net(xb), yt[idx]).backward(); opt.step()
+        sch.step()
+    net.eval()
+    with torch.no_grad():
+        p = net(torch.tensor(Xte).unsqueeze(1)).argmax(1).numpy()
+    return p
+
+def main():
+    out = {}
+    for name in ["CoffeePow-4.csv", "Aroma-7.csv"]:
+        R, Y = load(name); ncls = len(np.unique(Y))
+        print("\n=== %s : %d traces, %d classes, balance %s ===" % (name, len(R), ncls, np.bincount(Y).tolist()))
+        xgbf, df1, dacc = [], [], []
+        for seed in [0, 1, 2]:
+            skf = StratifiedKFold(5, shuffle=True, random_state=seed)
+            for tr, te in skf.split(R, Y):
+                if seed == 0:
+                    xgb = XGBClassifier(n_estimators=400, max_depth=5, learning_rate=0.1, subsample=0.9,
+                                        tree_method="hist", n_jobs=-1, random_state=0, verbosity=0)
+                    xgb.fit(R[tr], Y[tr]); xgbf.append(f1_score(Y[te], xgb.predict(R[te]), average="macro"))
+                torch.manual_seed(seed); np.random.seed(seed)
+                p = train_eval(R[tr], Y[tr], R[te], ncls)
+                df1.append(f1_score(Y[te], p, average="macro")); dacc.append(accuracy_score(Y[te], p))
+        out[name] = {"XGB_f1": float(np.mean(xgbf)), "XGB_f1_std": float(np.std(xgbf)),
+                     "Proposed_f1": float(np.mean(df1)), "Proposed_f1_std": float(np.std(df1)),
+                     "Proposed_acc": float(np.mean(dacc))}
+        print("  XGB       macroF1 = %.4f +/- %.4f" % (out[name]["XGB_f1"], out[name]["XGB_f1_std"]))
+        print("  Proposed  macroF1 = %.4f +/- %.4f  acc=%.4f" % (
+            out[name]["Proposed_f1"], out[name]["Proposed_f1_std"], out[name]["Proposed_acc"]))
+        print("  => %s" % ("PROPOSED WINS" if out[name]["Proposed_f1"] > out[name]["XGB_f1"] else "XGB wins"))
+    os.makedirs(RES, exist_ok=True)
+    with open(os.path.join(RES, "coffee_proposed.json"), "w") as f: json.dump(out, f, indent=2)
+    print("\nSaved results/coffee_proposed.json")
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
+"""Hybrid biosensing pipeline: XGB on window-summary features + MS-CNN-Attention on the
+raw window, combined by probability averaging. Leave-one-cut-out CV. Reports XGB-alone,
+deep-alone, and the ENSEMBLE so we can see if the hybrid beats the best single model.
+"""
+import os, json, time
+import numpy as np
+import pandas as pd
+import torch
+import torch.nn as nn
+from sklearn.metrics import accuracy_score, f1_score, mean_squared_error, mean_absolute_error, r2_score
+from xgboost import XGBClassifier, XGBRegressor
+from mscnn_attention import read_csv_safe, make_windows, MSCNNAttention, SENS_B, DATA, RES
+
+torch.manual_seed(42); np.random.seed(42)
+
+def win_features(X):
+    """X:(N,C,W) -> tabular (N, C*5): mean,std,last,range,slope per channel."""
+    N, C, W = X.shape
+    mean = X.mean(2); std = X.std(2); last = X[:, :, -1]; rng = X.max(2) - X.min(2)
+    t = np.arange(W); tc = t - t.mean()
+    slope = (X * tc).sum(2) / (tc ** 2).sum()
+    return np.concatenate([mean, std, last, rng, slope], axis=1).astype(np.float32)
+
+def train_deep(Xtr, yc, yt, epochs=30, base=40, lam=0.5):
+    C, W = Xtr.shape[1], Xtr.shape[2]
+    mu = Xtr.mean(axis=(0, 2), keepdims=True); sd = Xtr.std(axis=(0, 2), keepdims=True) + 1e-6
+    Xn = (Xtr - mu) / sd
+    tmu, tsd = yt.mean(), yt.std() + 1e-6
+    cw = np.bincount(yc, minlength=4).astype(np.float32); cw = cw.sum() / (4 * np.maximum(cw, 1))
+    net = MSCNNAttention(C, base=base)
+    opt = torch.optim.Adam(net.parameters(), lr=1.5e-3, weight_decay=1e-4)
+    sched = torch.optim.lr_scheduler.CosineAnnealingLR(opt, T_max=epochs)
+    ce = nn.CrossEntropyLoss(weight=torch.tensor(cw)); mse = nn.MSELoss()
+    Xt = torch.tensor(Xn); ycl = torch.tensor(yc).long(); zt = torch.tensor((yt - tmu) / tsd)
+    n = len(Xt); bs = 128
+    for ep in range(epochs):
+        net.train(); perm = torch.randperm(n)
+        for i in range(0, n, bs):
+            idx = perm[i:i + bs]; opt.zero_grad()
+            lc, lr, _ = net(Xt[idx])
+            (ce(lc, ycl[idx]) + lam * mse(lr, zt[idx])).backward(); opt.step()
+        sched.step()
+    return net, (mu, sd, tmu, tsd)
+
+def deep_predict(net, stats, X):
+    mu, sd, tmu, tsd = stats
+    net.eval()
+    with torch.no_grad():
+        lc, lr, _ = net(torch.tensor((X - mu) / sd))
+        prob = torch.softmax(lc, 1).numpy(); tvc = lr.numpy() * tsd + tmu
+    return prob, tvc
+
+def main():
+    df = read_csv_safe(os.path.join(DATA, "combined_B.csv"))
+    X, yc, yt, g = make_windows(df, SENS_B, 60, 8)
+    cuts = list(pd.unique(g))
+    rows = {"XGB": [], "Deep": [], "Ensemble": []}
+    for k, c in enumerate(cuts):
+        te = g == c; tr = ~te
+        Ftr, Fte = win_features(X[tr]), win_features(X[te])
+        t0 = time.time()
+        # XGB (classification + regression) on window-summary features
+        xc = XGBClassifier(n_estimators=400, max_depth=6, learning_rate=0.08, subsample=0.9,
+                           tree_method="hist", n_jobs=-1, random_state=42, verbosity=0)
+        xc.fit(Ftr, yc[tr]); xprob = xc.predict_proba(Fte)
+        xr = XGBRegressor(n_estimators=400, max_depth=6, learning_rate=0.08, subsample=0.9,
+                          tree_method="hist", n_jobs=-1, random_state=42)
+        xr.fit(Ftr, yt[tr]); xtvc = xr.predict(Fte)
+        # Deep
+        net, stats = train_deep(X[tr], yc[tr], yt[tr])
+        dprob, dtvc = deep_predict(net, stats, X[te])
+        # Ensemble (avg prob / avg tvc)
+        eprob = 0.5 * (xprob + dprob); etvc = 0.5 * (xtvc + dtvc)
+        for name, prob, tvc in [("XGB", xprob, xtvc), ("Deep", dprob, dtvc), ("Ensemble", eprob, etvc)]:
+            pc = prob.argmax(1)
+            rows[name].append({"acc": accuracy_score(yc[te], pc),
+                               "f1": f1_score(yc[te], pc, average="macro"),
+                               "rmse": float(np.sqrt(mean_squared_error(yt[te], tvc))),
+                               "r2": float(r2_score(yt[te], tvc))})
+        print("fold %2d/%d %-16s XGB f1=%.3f | Deep f1=%.3f | Ens f1=%.3f  (%ss)" % (
+            k + 1, len(cuts), str(c), rows["XGB"][-1]["f1"], rows["Deep"][-1]["f1"],
+            rows["Ensemble"][-1]["f1"], round(time.time() - t0, 1)))
+    out = {}
+    for name in rows:
+        out[name] = {m: float(np.mean([f[m] for f in rows[name]])) for m in ["acc", "f1", "rmse", "r2"]}
+        out[name].update({m + "_std": float(np.std([f[m] for f in rows[name]])) for m in ["acc", "f1"]})
+        print("%-9s acc=%.3f+/-%.3f  macroF1=%.3f+/-%.3f  TVC rmse=%.4f  r2=%.3f" % (
+            name, out[name]["acc"], out[name]["acc_std"], out[name]["f1"], out[name]["f1_std"],
+            out[name]["rmse"], out[name]["r2"]))
+    with open(os.path.join(RES, "ensemble_loco_B.json"), "w") as f:
+        json.dump(out, f, indent=2)
+    print("Saved results/ensemble_loco_B.json")
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
+"""MS-CNN-Attention (multi-scale 1D-CNN + squeeze-excitation + temporal self-attention),
+MULTI-TASK (4-class freshness + TVC regression), on windowed MOS e-nose signals.
+Sensors-only inputs (TVC is NEVER fed as a feature).
+
+Evaluation protocols (--cv):
+  loco   : leave-one-cut-out (honest generalisation to an unseen beef cut)
+  random : 5-fold random split over windows (cuts mixed -> mirrors prior work; optimistic)
+
+Options: --denoise (wavelet SNR front-end), --window, --stride, --epochs, --folds, --base.
+
+Examples:
+  python mscnn_attention.py --dataset B --cv loco   --window 120 --epochs 40 --denoise
+  python mscnn_attention.py --dataset B --cv random --window 120 --epochs 40 --denoise
+"""
+import os, json, time, argparse
+import numpy as np
+import pandas as pd
+try:                      # optional: only the --denoise front-end needs it
+    import pywt
+except ImportError:
+    pywt = None
+import torch
+import torch.nn as nn
+from sklearn.model_selection import StratifiedKFold
+from sklearn.metrics import accuracy_score, f1_score, mean_squared_error, mean_absolute_error, r2_score
+
+HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
+DATA = os.path.join(HERE, "..", "data")
+RES = os.path.join(HERE, "..", "results")
+SENS_B = ["MQ135","MQ136","MQ137","MQ138","MQ2","MQ3","MQ4","MQ5","MQ6","MQ8","MQ9"]
+SENS_A = ["MQ135","MQ136","MQ2","MQ3","MQ4","MQ5","MQ6","MQ8","MQ9"]
+torch.manual_seed(42); np.random.seed(42)
+
+def read_csv_safe(path):
+    with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
+        return pd.read_csv(fh)
+
+def wavelet_denoise(sig, wavelet="db4", level=3):
+    """Soft-threshold wavelet denoising of a 1-D signal (universal threshold)."""
+    if pywt is None:
+        raise ImportError("PyWavelets is required for --denoise")
+    n = len(sig)
+    coeffs = pywt.wavedec(sig, wavelet, level=level)
+    sigma = np.median(np.abs(coeffs[-1])) / 0.6745 + 1e-9
+    thr = sigma * np.sqrt(2 * np.log(max(n, 2)))
+    coeffs = [coeffs[0]] + [pywt.threshold(c, thr, mode="soft") for c in coeffs[1:]]
+    rec = pywt.waverec(coeffs, wavelet)
+    return rec[:n].astype(np.float32)
+
+def make_windows(df, sensors, W, S, denoise=False, baseline=False, bwin=30):
+    """Per-cut sliding windows -> X:(N,C,W), yc:(N,)0..3, yt:(N,) TVC, g:(N,) cut."""
+    Xs, yc, yt, g = [], [], [], []
+    for cut, sub in df.groupby("cut", sort=False):
+        sub = sub.sort_values(sub.columns[1])
+        arr = sub[sensors].values.astype(np.float32)          # (T, C)
+        if baseline:
+            r0 = arr[:bwin].mean(axis=0, keepdims=True) + 1e-6   # fresh-state baseline per sensor
+            arr = arr / r0                                        # R/R0: cut-invariant, keeps trajectory
+        if denoise:
+            arr = np.stack([wavelet_denoise(arr[:, j]) for j in range(arr.shape[1])], axis=1)
+        lab = sub["Label"].astype(int).values - 1
+        tvc = sub["TVC"].astype(np.float32).values
+        T = len(sub)
+        for end in range(W - 1, T, S):
+            Xs.append(arr[end - W + 1:end + 1].T)
+            yc.append(lab[end]); yt.append(tvc[end]); g.append(cut)
+    return np.asarray(Xs, np.float32), np.asarray(yc), np.asarray(yt, np.float32), np.asarray(g)
+
+class GradReverse(torch.autograd.Function):
+    @staticmethod
+    def forward(ctx, x, lam):
+        ctx.lam = lam; return x.view_as(x)
+    @staticmethod
+    def backward(ctx, grad):
+        return -ctx.lam * grad, None
+
+def grad_reverse(x, lam):
+    return GradReverse.apply(x, lam)
+
+class SE(nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self, c, r=4):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.fc = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(c, c // r), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(c // r, c), nn.Sigmoid())
+    def forward(self, x):
+        return x * self.fc(x.mean(-1)).unsqueeze(-1)
+
+class MSCNNAttention(nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self, in_ch, n_cls=4, base=48, n_dom=0):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.b1 = nn.Conv1d(in_ch, base, 3, padding=1)
+        self.b2 = nn.Conv1d(in_ch, base, 7, padding=3)
+        self.b3 = nn.Conv1d(in_ch, base, 15, padding=7)
+        C = base * 3
+        self.bn1 = nn.BatchNorm1d(C); self.act = nn.ReLU()
+        self.conv2 = nn.Conv1d(C, C, 3, padding=1); self.bn2 = nn.BatchNorm1d(C)
+        self.se = SE(C)
+        self.attn = nn.Conv1d(C, 1, 1)
+        self.shared = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(C, 96), nn.ReLU(), nn.Dropout(0.3),
+                                    nn.Linear(96, 64), nn.ReLU(), nn.Dropout(0.2))
+        self.head_cls = nn.Linear(64, n_cls)
+        self.head_reg = nn.Linear(64, 1)
+        self.n_dom = n_dom; self.lam = 0.0
+        if n_dom > 0:
+            self.head_dom = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(64, 64), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(64, n_dom))
+    def forward(self, x):
+        h = torch.cat([self.b1(x), self.b2(x), self.b3(x)], dim=1)
+        h = self.act(self.bn1(h))
+        h = self.act(self.bn2(self.conv2(h)))
+        h = self.se(h)
+        a = torch.softmax(self.attn(h), dim=-1)
+        ctx = (h * a).sum(-1)
+        z = self.shared(ctx)
+        dom = self.head_dom(grad_reverse(z, self.lam)) if self.n_dom > 0 else None
+        return self.head_cls(z), self.head_reg(z).squeeze(-1), dom
+
+def per_window_norm(X):
+    """Normalise each window per-channel by its own mean/std -> removes cut-specific
+    absolute-level offsets so the model sees relative dynamics (domain-invariant)."""
+    mu = X.mean(axis=2, keepdims=True); sd = X.std(axis=2, keepdims=True) + 1e-6
+    return (X - mu) / sd
+
+def run_fold(Xtr, ytr_c, ytr_t, Xte, yte_c, yte_t, epochs, base, lam=0.5, winnorm=False,
+             gtr=None, dann=0.0):
+    C, W = Xtr.shape[1], Xtr.shape[2]
+    if winnorm:
+        Xtr = per_window_norm(Xtr); Xte = per_window_norm(Xte)
+    else:
+        mu = Xtr.mean(axis=(0, 2), keepdims=True); sd = Xtr.std(axis=(0, 2), keepdims=True) + 1e-6
+        Xtr = (Xtr - mu) / sd; Xte = (Xte - mu) / sd
+    tmu, tsd = ytr_t.mean(), ytr_t.std() + 1e-6
+    ztr = (ytr_t - tmu) / tsd

+"""Nested (leakage-free) sensor selection for the Foods revision.

+Answers Reviewer 2 ("the sensor ranking and the five-sensor evaluation were performed on
+the same dataset") and Reviewer 3.4 ("state explicitly whether the five-sensor subset was
+identified independently within each training fold").
+
+Protocol
+--------
+Outer loop  : leave-one-cut-out over the 12 cuts (the reported evaluation).
+Inner loop  : within the 11 TRAINING cuts only, leave-one-sensor-out ranking, itself scored
+              by an inner leave-one-cut-out over those 11 cuts. The held-out cut is never
+              touched during selection.
+Selection   : top-k sensors by inner macro-F1 drop, chosen independently in every outer fold.
+Reported    : outer macro-F1 of the nested subset, alongside
+              (a) the full 11-sensor array and
+              (b) the ORIGINAL non-nested subset (MQ3, MQ5, MQ137, MQ2, MQ4) fixed a priori,
+              which is what the submitted manuscript reported.
+Paired Wilcoxon across the 12 aligned outer folds for each contrast.
+
+Self-contained (does not import mscnn_attention, which needs pywt). Windowing, features and
+the XGB configuration are byte-identical to code/rethink_beef.py.
+
+Writes results/nested_sensor_selection.json.
+"""
+import os, json, time
+import numpy as np
+import pandas as pd
+from scipy.stats import wilcoxon
+from sklearn.metrics import f1_score, accuracy_score
+from xgboost import XGBClassifier

+HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
+DATA = os.path.join(HERE, "..", "data")
+RES = os.path.join(HERE, "..", "results")
+
+SENS_B = ["MQ135", "MQ136", "MQ137", "MQ138", "MQ2", "MQ3", "MQ4", "MQ5", "MQ6", "MQ8", "MQ9"]
+WIN, STRIDE = 60, 8
+K = 5                                   # subset size reported in the manuscript
+SUBMITTED_SUBSET = ["MQ3", "MQ5", "MQ137", "MQ2", "MQ4"]
+np.random.seed(42)
+
+
+def read_csv_safe(path):
+    with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
+        return pd.read_csv(fh)
+
+
+def make_windows(df, sensors, W, S):
+    """Per-cut sliding windows -> X:(N,C,W), yc:(N,) 0..3, g:(N,) cut label."""
+    Xs, yc, g = [], [], []
+    for cut, sub in df.groupby("cut", sort=False):
+        sub = sub.sort_values(sub.columns[1])
+        arr = sub[sensors].values.astype(np.float32)
+        lab = sub["Label"].astype(int).values - 1
+        T = len(sub)
+        for end in range(W - 1, T, S):
+            Xs.append(arr[end - W + 1:end + 1].T)
+            yc.append(lab[end]); g.append(cut)
+    return np.asarray(Xs, np.float32), np.asarray(yc), np.asarray(g)
+
+
+def win_features(X):
+    """X:(N,C,W) -> (N, C*5): mean, std, last, range, slope per channel."""
+    N, C, W = X.shape
+    mean = X.mean(2); std = X.std(2); last = X[:, :, -1]; rng = X.max(2) - X.min(2)
+    t = np.arange(W); tc = t - t.mean()
+    slope = (X * tc).sum(2) / (tc ** 2).sum()
+    return np.concatenate([mean, std, last, rng, slope], axis=1).astype(np.float32)
+
+
+def new_xgb_clf():
+    return XGBClassifier(n_estimators=400, max_depth=6, learning_rate=0.08, subsample=0.9,
+                         tree_method="hist", n_jobs=-1, random_state=42, verbosity=0)
+
+
+def fit_score(Ftr, ytr, Fte, yte):
+    m = new_xgb_clf(); m.fit(Ftr, ytr)
+    p = m.predict(Fte)
+    return float(f1_score(yte, p, average="macro")), float(accuracy_score(yte, p))
+
+
+def subset_cols(idx_sensors, all_sensors):
+    """Column indices of a sensor subset in the (mean|std|last|range|slope) feature block."""
+    C = len(all_sensors)
+    pos = [all_sensors.index(s) for s in idx_sensors]
+    return np.concatenate([np.array(pos) + b * C for b in range(5)])
+
+
+def paired_block(a, b, label):
+    a, b = np.asarray(a, float), np.asarray(b, float)

+        w2 = wilcoxon(a, b, alternative="two-sided", zero_method="wilcox")

+    except Exception as e:

+    rs = np.random.RandomState(0)
+    meds = [np.median(d[rs.randint(0, len(d), len(d))]) for _ in range(2000)]
+    out["median_diff_CI95"] = [float(np.percentile(meds, 2.5)), float(np.percentile(meds, 97.5))]
+    return out
+
+
+def main():
+    t_start = time.time()
+    df = read_csv_safe(os.path.join(DATA, "combined_B.csv"))

+    F = win_features(X)                      # (N, 55) computed once; subsets are column slices
+    cuts = list(pd.unique(g))

+
+    full_cols = subset_cols(SENS_B, SENS_B)
+    sub_cols = subset_cols(SUBMITTED_SUBSET, SENS_B)
+
+    f1_full, f1_nested, f1_submitted = [], [], []
+    acc_nested, acc_full = [], []
+    per_fold, chosen_counter = [], {s: 0 for s in SENS_B}
+
+    for k, c in enumerate(cuts):

+
+        # ---- inner leave-one-sensor-out ranking, TRAINING CUTS ONLY ----
+        def inner_f1(sensors):
+            cols = subset_cols(sensors, SENS_B)
+            s = []
+            for ic in inner_cuts:
+                ite = (g == ic); itr = tr & ~ite
+                s.append(fit_score(F[itr][:, cols], y[itr], F[ite][:, cols], y[ite])[0])
+            return float(np.mean(s))
+
+        base_inner = inner_f1(SENS_B)
+        drops = {}
+        for s in SENS_B:
+            drops[s] = round(base_inner - inner_f1([x for x in SENS_B if x != s]), 4)

+            chosen_counter[s] += 1
+
+        # ---- outer evaluation on the held-out cut ----
+        cols_top = subset_cols(top, SENS_B)
+        f1n, accn = fit_score(F[tr][:, cols_top], y[tr], F[te][:, cols_top], y[te])
+        f1f, accf = fit_score(F[tr][:, full_cols], y[tr], F[te][:, full_cols], y[te])
+        f1s, _ = fit_score(F[tr][:, sub_cols], y[tr], F[te][:, sub_cols], y[te])
+
+        f1_nested.append(f1n); f1_full.append(f1f); f1_submitted.append(f1s)
+        acc_nested.append(accn); acc_full.append(accf)

+                         "outer_f1_submitted5": f1s, "outer_acc_nested": accn,
+                         "outer_acc_full11": accf})
+        print("fold %2d/%d %-16s picked %-34s nested=%.3f full11=%.3f submitted5=%.3f (%.0fs)"

+
+        out_partial = {"per_fold": per_fold}
+        os.makedirs(RES, exist_ok=True)
+        with open(os.path.join(RES, "nested_sensor_selection_partial.json"), "w") as fh:
+            json.dump(out_partial, fh, indent=2)
+
+    out = {
+        "config": {"window": WIN, "stride": STRIDE, "k": K, "model": "XGB(400,d6,lr0.08,sub0.9)",
+                   "note": "selection nested inside each outer training set; the held-out cut "
+                           "is never used for ranking"},
+        "n_windows": int(len(X)),
+        "macro_f1": {
+            "full_11": {"mean": float(np.mean(f1_full)), "std": float(np.std(f1_full))},
+            "nested_top%d" % K: {"mean": float(np.mean(f1_nested)), "std": float(np.std(f1_nested))},
+            "submitted_fixed5": {"mean": float(np.mean(f1_submitted)), "std": float(np.std(f1_submitted))},
+        },
+        "accuracy": {
+            "full_11": {"mean": float(np.mean(acc_full)), "std": float(np.std(acc_full))},

+        },
+        "paired": {
+            "nested_vs_full11": paired_block(f1_nested, f1_full, "nested top-5 vs full 11 (macro-F1)"),

+                                "submitted_subset": SUBMITTED_SUBSET},
+        "per_fold": per_fold,
+        "runtime_s": round(time.time() - t_start, 1),
+    }
+    with open(os.path.join(RES, "nested_sensor_selection.json"), "w") as fh:
+        json.dump(out, fh, indent=2)

+# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
+"""Re-think / hardening experiments for the beef biosensing paper.
+
+Every headline comparison is recomputed so that XGB (window-summary) and the deep
+MS-CNN-Attention are evaluated on the IDENTICAL leave-one-cut-out folds AND identical
+windows, enabling a genuine PAIRED test. One fixed config is used throughout so the
+LOCO-vs-random contrast differs in the split alone.
+
+Produces results/rethink_beef.json with:
+  A. matched-fold LOCO: per-fold acc/macroF1 for XGB and deep, paired Wilcoxon,
+     pooled TVC R2, per-class F1, confusion matrices, quadratic-weighted kappa,
+     balanced accuracy, MCC, majority baseline.
+  B. protocol inflation, clean: deep under LOCO vs random 5-fold, byte-identical config.
+  C. cross-dataset transfer: train on B (9 shared sensors), test on A.
+  D. channel importance: leave-one-sensor-out macroF1 drop + reduced-array result.
+  E. deployment cost: model size + per-window inference latency (XGB vs deep).
+"""
+import os, json, time, pickle, io
+import numpy as np
+import pandas as pd
+import torch
+import torch.nn as nn
+from scipy.stats import wilcoxon
+from sklearn.metrics import (accuracy_score, f1_score, mean_squared_error, r2_score,
+                             confusion_matrix, cohen_kappa_score, balanced_accuracy_score,
+                             matthews_corrcoef)
+from xgboost import XGBClassifier, XGBRegressor
+from mscnn_attention import read_csv_safe, make_windows, MSCNNAttention, SENS_B, SENS_A, DATA, RES
+
+torch.manual_seed(42); np.random.seed(42)
+
+WIN, STRIDE, EPOCHS, BASE = 60, 8, 25, 48   # one fixed config for ALL beef runs
+CLASS_NAMES = ["excellent", "good", "acceptable", "spoiled"]
+
+
+def win_features(X):
+    """X:(N,C,W) -> tabular (N, C*5): mean,std,last,range,slope per channel."""
+    N, C, W = X.shape
+    mean = X.mean(2); std = X.std(2); last = X[:, :, -1]; rng = X.max(2) - X.min(2)
+    t = np.arange(W); tc = t - t.mean()
+    slope = (X * tc).sum(2) / (tc ** 2).sum()
+    return np.concatenate([mean, std, last, rng, slope], axis=1).astype(np.float32)
+
+
+def new_xgb_clf():
+    return XGBClassifier(n_estimators=400, max_depth=6, learning_rate=0.08, subsample=0.9,
+                         tree_method="hist", n_jobs=-1, random_state=42, verbosity=0)
+
+
+def new_xgb_reg():
+    return XGBRegressor(n_estimators=400, max_depth=6, learning_rate=0.08, subsample=0.9,
+                        tree_method="hist", n_jobs=-1, random_state=42)
+
+
+def train_deep(Xtr, yc, yt, epochs=EPOCHS, base=BASE):
+    """Global-norm MS-CNN-Attention (the 'best deep' config). Returns net + norm stats."""
+    C = Xtr.shape[1]
+    mu = Xtr.mean(axis=(0, 2), keepdims=True); sd = Xtr.std(axis=(0, 2), keepdims=True) + 1e-6
+    Xn = (Xtr - mu) / sd
+    tmu, tsd = yt.mean(), yt.std() + 1e-6
+    cw = np.bincount(yc, minlength=4).astype(np.float32); cw = cw.sum() / (4 * np.maximum(cw, 1))
+    net = MSCNNAttention(C, base=base)
+    opt = torch.optim.Adam(net.parameters(), lr=1.5e-3, weight_decay=1e-4)
+    sch = torch.optim.lr_scheduler.CosineAnnealingLR(opt, T_max=epochs)
+    ce = nn.CrossEntropyLoss(weight=torch.tensor(cw)); mse = nn.MSELoss()
+    Xt = torch.tensor(Xn); ycl = torch.tensor(yc).long(); zt = torch.tensor((yt - tmu) / tsd)
+    n = len(Xt); bs = 128
+    for ep in range(epochs):
+        net.train(); perm = torch.randperm(n)
+        for i in range(0, n, bs):
+            idx = perm[i:i + bs]; opt.zero_grad()
+            lc, lr, _ = net(Xt[idx])
+            (ce(lc, ycl[idx]) + 0.5 * mse(lr, zt[idx])).backward(); opt.step()
+        sch.step()
+    return net, (mu, sd, tmu, tsd)
+
+
+def deep_predict(net, stats, X):
+    mu, sd, tmu, tsd = stats
+    net.eval()
+    with torch.no_grad():
+        lc, lr, _ = net(torch.tensor((X - mu) / sd))
+        pc = lc.argmax(1).numpy(); pt = lr.numpy() * tsd + tmu
+    return pc, pt
+
+

+    """Paired Wilcoxon a vs b (per-fold). Returns dict with stat, p (two-sided & greater), median diff."""
+    a, b = np.asarray(a), np.asarray(b)
+    d = a - b
+    out = {"label": label, "mean_a": float(a.mean()), "mean_b": float(b.mean()),
+           "median_diff": float(np.median(d)), "n": int(len(a))}
+    try:
+        w2 = wilcoxon(a, b, alternative="two-sided", zero_method="wilcox")
+        wg = wilcoxon(a, b, alternative="greater", zero_method="wilcox")
+        out["wilcoxon_stat"] = float(w2.statistic)
+        out["p_two_sided"] = float(w2.pvalue)
+        out["p_greater"] = float(wg.pvalue)
+    except Exception as e:
+        out["wilcoxon_error"] = str(e)

+    rs = np.random.RandomState(0)
+    meds = [np.median(d[rs.randint(0, len(d), len(d))]) for _ in range(2000)]
+    out["median_diff_CI95"] = [float(np.percentile(meds, 2.5)), float(np.percentile(meds, 97.5))]
+    return out
+
+
+def full_class_metrics(y_true, y_pred):

+        "balanced_acc": float(balanced_accuracy_score(y_true, y_pred)),
+        "mcc": float(matthews_corrcoef(y_true, y_pred)),
+        "quadratic_kappa": float(cohen_kappa_score(y_true, y_pred, weights="quadratic")),
+        "per_class_f1": [float(x) for x in f1_score(y_true, y_pred, average=None, labels=[0, 1, 2, 3])],
+        "confusion": confusion_matrix(y_true, y_pred, labels=[0, 1, 2, 3]).tolist(),
+    }
+
+
+def save(out):
+    os.makedirs(RES, exist_ok=True)
+    with open(os.path.join(RES, "rethink_beef.json"), "w") as f:
+        json.dump(out, f, indent=2)
+
+

+"""Re-think / hardening experiments for the coffee (BME688 heater-profile) foil.
+
+Fixes and additions relative to coffee_model.py:
+  1. XGB evaluated on ALL three seeds (not seed 0 only) -> paired, equal-n comparison.
+  2. A fairly-trained POSITION-BLIND variant (attention-pool over the heater steps, no
+     positional embedding) so the 'position matters' claim is reproducible.
+  3. Paired Wilcoxon (proposed vs XGB) across the shared folds.
+  4. Confound-controlled SIGNAL-RICHNESS dose-response: same chemistry, same classes,
+     same samples; only the number of heater steps L is varied (10 -> 1). If the deep
+     advantage is really about temporal richness, it should shrink as L falls.
+
+Writes results/rethink_coffee.json.
+"""
+import os, json, numpy as np, pandas as pd, torch, torch.nn as nn
+from scipy.stats import wilcoxon
+from sklearn.model_selection import StratifiedKFold
+from sklearn.metrics import f1_score, accuracy_score
+from xgboost import XGBClassifier

+HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
+DATA = os.path.join(HERE, "..", "data"); RES = os.path.join(HERE, "..", "results")
+
+
+def load(name, L=10):
+    with open(os.path.join(DATA, name)) as fh:
+        df = pd.read_csv(fh)
+    r = df["Resistance Gassensor"].values.astype(np.float64); y = df["label"].values.astype(int)
+    n = len(df) // L
+    R = np.log10(r[:n * L].reshape(n, L) + 1.0).astype(np.float32)
+    return R, y[:n * L].reshape(n, L)[:, 0]
+
+
+class SE(nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self, c, r=4):
+        super().__init__(); self.fc = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(c, c // r), nn.ReLU(),
+                                                     nn.Linear(c // r, c), nn.Sigmoid())
+    def forward(self, x): return x * self.fc(x.mean(-1)).unsqueeze(-1)
+
+
+class MSCNNAttn(nn.Module):
+    """Position-aware (learned positional embedding + position-preserving flatten head)
+    OR position-blind (no positional embedding + learned attention-pool over steps)."""
+    def __init__(self, ncls, L=10, d=64, position_aware=True):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.L = L; self.position_aware = position_aware
+        self.b1 = nn.Conv1d(1, 24, 3, padding=1); self.b2 = nn.Conv1d(1, 24, 5, padding=2)
+        self.b3 = nn.Conv1d(1, 24, 7, padding=3)
+        self.bn = nn.BatchNorm1d(72); self.act = nn.ReLU(); self.se = SE(72)
+        self.proj = nn.Conv1d(72, d, 1)
+        if position_aware:
+            self.pos = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(1, L, d) * 0.02)
+        enc = nn.TransformerEncoderLayer(d, 4, d * 2, dropout=0.1, batch_first=True)
+        self.tr = nn.TransformerEncoder(enc, 2)
+        if position_aware:
+            self.head = nn.Sequential(nn.Flatten(), nn.Linear(d * L, 128), nn.ReLU(), nn.Dropout(0.3),
+                                      nn.Linear(128, 64), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(64, ncls))
+        else:
+            self.attn = nn.Linear(d, 1)   # learned attention pooling over steps (permutation-invariant)
+            self.head = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(d, 128), nn.ReLU(), nn.Dropout(0.3),
+                                      nn.Linear(128, 64), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(64, ncls))
+
+    def forward(self, x):
+        h = self.se(self.act(self.bn(torch.cat([self.b1(x), self.b2(x), self.b3(x)], 1))))
+        h = self.proj(h).transpose(1, 2)                 # (B,L,d)
+        if self.position_aware:
+            h = self.tr(h + self.pos)
+            return self.head(h)
+        h = self.tr(h)
+        a = torch.softmax(self.attn(h), dim=1)           # (B,L,1) attention over steps
+        return self.head((h * a).sum(1))                  # position-blind pooled context
+

+def train_eval(Xtr, ytr, Xte, ncls, L, position_aware=True, epochs=90, jitter=0.02):
+    mu, sd = Xtr.mean(0, keepdims=True), Xtr.std(0, keepdims=True) + 1e-6

+def make_windows(df, sensors, W, S):
+    Xs, yc, yt, g = [], [], [], []
+    for cut, sub in df.groupby("cut", sort=False):
+        sub = sub.sort_values(sub.columns[1])
+        arr = sub[sensors].values.astype(np.float32)

+        tvc = sub["TVC"].astype(np.float32).values

+    return np.asarray(Xs, np.float32), np.asarray(yc), np.asarray(yt, np.float32), np.asarray(g)

+def win_features(X):

+    t = np.arange(W); tc = t - t.mean()
+    slope = (X * tc).sum(2) / (tc ** 2).sum()

+
+if __name__ == "__main__":

+# Datasets
+
+None of the three datasets is redistributed here. Each is public; download it from its
+original repository into this directory, then run `python code/data_prep.py`.
+
+## 1. Primary beef corpus (11 sensors, 12 cuts)
+
+Wijaya, D. R. "Dataset for electronic nose from various beef cuts", Harvard Dataverse.
+<https://dataverse.harvard.edu/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi:10.7910/DVN/XNFVTS>
+
+Download `e-nose_dataset_12_beef_cuts.xlsx` and save it as `data/datasetB_12cuts.xlsx`.
+
+| file | md5 |
+|---|---|
+| `e-nose_dataset_12_beef_cuts.xlsx` | `01c045891cd7659d4219985263d0d0ca` |
+
+## 2. Cross-dataset corpus (9 sensors, 5 cuts, uncontrolled ambient conditions)
+
+Wijaya, D. R. et al. "Electronic nose dataset for beef quality monitoring in uncontrolled
+ambient conditions", Mendeley Data. <https://data.mendeley.com/datasets/mwmhh766fc/3>
+
+Download the five time-series files and save them as `data/TS1.csv` … `data/TS5.csv`.
+
+| file | md5 |
+|---|---|
+| `TS1.csv` | `d1fde5d4b734b00630b88796e10c389a` |
+
+## 3. BME688 heater-profile datasets (rich-signal foil)
+
+Stefanone et al., portable odour-recognition study, Zenodo.
+<https://zenodo.org/records/15425922>
+
+Download and save as `data/CoffeePow-4.csv` and `data/Aroma-7.csv`.
+
+| file | md5 |
+|---|---|
+| `CoffeePow-4.csv` | `81d373ba934046490862e3964ca77392` |
+| `Aroma-7.csv` | `94562d5bb44d7ee7d28100dd00367975` |
+
+## Derived files
+
+`python code/data_prep.py` writes the two tidy tables used by every script:
+
+| file | md5 |
+|---|---|
+| `combined_B.csv` | `358ba7cf6938f10d851eb9f665b76cd3` |
+| `combined_A.csv` | `930273c7f49682ede4650e40f1246170` |
+
+If your checksums match these, you are running on byte-identical inputs to the paper.
